dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Hope the Akademiya will not interfere with adventurers' activity too much...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Hi, I'm Kamal, a Branch Master of the Adventurers' Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: I'm a former mariner. I can give you some practical tips if you want to set sail on an adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: If you want to go somewhere else in Sumeru, I can show the way as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Have a good day and a safe adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Much obliged.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Sumeru City was built on the Divine Tree, with the upper level for the Akademiya and the lower level for the common folks. Move up if you seek further education or get a promotion. For a steady life pace, Grand Bazaar is your choice.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Researchers led by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata cultivated a large rainforest right next to Sumeru City, which helped Sumeru survive the difficult times in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: But it's not a good idea to delve too deep into the rainforest. Beasts and The Withering can be deadly. Be sure to call a Forest Ranger for help in case of danger.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: There are plenty of places to stay near the rainforest. The Gandharva Ville where Forest Rangers and Vanara gather, and the tranquil Vimara Village. You name it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Further south is Port Ormos, the largest import and export port in Sumeru. Most people who travel to Sumeru by water would enter through the port.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Beyond the rainforest...

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Going west, across the Caravan Ribat, you will reach the desert. Somewhere in the desert lies King Deshret, a spot many Adventurers often beat a path to.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: But the environment is treacherous, and even a small sandstorm can be a terribly foul experience. If you must go, you'd better find a reliable guide at Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Aaru Village is on the edge of the desert, and is friendly to tourists and traveling scholars.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: There seems to be an abandoned medical facility up there, and it was sealed off by the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: I know adventurers are mostly curious and don't really like the Akademiya or the Eremites bossing around with their plans...

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Still, that doesn't look like a great place for travel, so I don't advise you to be rash with your actions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Much obliged, then.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Sumeru City was built on the Divine Tree, with the upper levels being meant for the Akademiya and the lower levels for the common folks. Move up if you seek further education or get a promotion, but if you want to take life steady, the Grand Bazaar is the choice for you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Researchers led by Dendro Archon cultivated a large rainforest right next to Sumeru City, which has helped Sumeru survive difficult times in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: But it's not a good idea to delve too deep into the rainforest. An encounter with beasts and The Withering within can prove deadly, so be sure to call a Forest Ranger for help in case of any danger.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: There are plenty of places to stay near the rainforest, such as Gandharva Ville, where the Forest Rangers and Vanara gather, and the tranquil Vimara Village.

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Further south is Port Ormos, the largest import and export port in Sumeru. Most people who travel to Sumeru by water enter that way.
